text:
Maya R.: Heads-up — after shading a 3rd-party JSON lib into the Kotlin client fat JAR, staging is showing streaming responses hang (ndjson) and an intermittent auth header drop on 302 redirects. Anyone run into classloader/relocation weirdness that looks like this?

Aj Patel: Yup, that pattern screams partial-relocation. If some packages are relocated and others are not, you can end up with mixed jackson/gson classes at runtime. Can you paste your shadowJar block + a tiny stack trace or logs?

Maya R.: Minimal trace from staging: "NoSuchMethodError: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonFactory.createParser(Ljava/io/InputStream;)Lcom/fasterxml/jackson/core/JsonParser;" then ndjson consumer just stops emitting tokens (no exception). Build snippet: 
```gradle
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.fasterxml', 'shadow.com.fasterxml' // I tried this but maybe missed subpackages
  // I didn't relocate com.google.gson initially
}
```

Kevin L.: Couple things to check: 1) relocate the full package roots (com.fasterxml.jackson, com.fasterxml.jackson.core, com.fasterxml.jackson.databind), not just `com.fasterxml`. 2) If you use ServiceLoader-based modules (e.g., jackson-databind module discovery), you may need to relocate META-INF/services entries or rewrite them so the ServiceLoader finds the relocated impls. 3) OkHttp note: if your auth interceptor runs after the redirect/follow logic, the header can be dropped on 302 -> ensure auth runs before redirection or set `Authenticator` properly.

Sam O.: Quick repro trick: run the shaded jar with `-verbose:class` and grep for which `com.fasterxml` classes are loaded and from which JAR. Also try `jdeps` on the final JAR to see unresolved references.

Maya R.: Good call on ServiceLoader. I forgot to rewrite `META-INF/services`. For now I pushed these changes in a tiny branch: 1) relocate full roots for jackson and gson, 2) use Shadow plugin's `transform(ServiceFileTransformer)` to merge/relocate service files, 3) reorder OkHttp interceptors so auth runs first.

Aj Patel: Nice. For the ndjson hang specifically, also ensure your client-side parser version matches the server serialization behavior — mixed jackson-core/databind versions can lead to streaming API mismatches that block on token boundaries. If you can add an integration test that opens an ndjson stream and reads a few lines then closes, that'll catch regressions.

ci-bot: Deploy to staging ran: tests:unit ✅, tests:integration flaky-1 (timeout reading stream) — investigating logs.

Maya R.: Deploying updated jar to staging now with the relocations + service-file transform. If staging looks green I'll open the PR for review and include the integration test Aj suggested.

Kevin L.: Ping me on the PR, I can check the ServiceLoader changes and the interceptor ordering. Also update the docs/FAQ about shading pitfalls so future client libs avoid this.

Maya R.: Will do. Thanks all :rocket:

Aj Patel: Also add a small note in the gradle script: `shadowJar { minimize() }` only if you understand consequences — sometimes minimizing can drop ServiceLoader metadata.

Sam O.: FYI if anyone else hits it — reason this is subtle: a relocated class and an unrelocated class with the same binary name but different classloader can lead to `NoSuchMethodError` even though the symbols look present at compile time.

Kevin L.: :thumbsup:
